summary: Clatsop County tree crow's nest of 1921 on Sugarloaf Mountain, tried as a lookout, abandoned in the 1930s; the register lists it as gone. Private timberland.

facts.design: Tree crow's nest, with a patrol point on nearby rocks
facts.status_note: The register lists it as gone. The FFLA Oregon county list says Abandoned.

access.note: A climbing trip report says the mountain sits in private timberland.

events.note: Tree crow's nest built on the site, with a patrol point on the nearby rocks
Aircraft warning station proposed for the summit; the letter calls the plan impractical
Registered October 15, 2019, on the nomination of Tammy McLeod

evidence.supports: crow's nest and camp in 1921, abandoned in the 1930s
firelookout.com gives a location nine miles NNE of Newhalem, which does not fit the Clatsop County location
station tried out as a lookout with temporary quarters; abandoned for fog reasons
evidence.quote: A number of years ago this point was tried out as a lookout station; but due to the fact that the lookout was unable to see for approximately 50 percent of the time because of coastal fogs, the station was abandoned for lookout purposes.

evidence.supports: the earlier try-out used only temporary quarters
evidence.quote: As only temporary quarters were provided for the lookout during this try-out period, the establishment of a year-round station on Sugar Loaf would require a full set of buildings and construction of approximately five miles of telephone line.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com gives nine miles NNE of Newhalem, which would fall in Washington State, while the same page, the register and the FFLA list place the site in Clatsop County, Oregon. The Newhalem figure is treated as an error and is not used.
The register says gone; the FFLA list says Abandoned; firelookout.com and SummitPost say abandoned in the 1930s. None says the lookout still stands, so the register's gone is kept.

notes_for_editor: PROBABLE DUPLICATE: us-or-sugarloaf-mountain-clatsop-county already has a story and research for this same register entry (US 1768, ODF Clatsop FPA, 871 m, 1921 crow's nest). That record carries the Curry County point's coordinates (42.83802, -124.23487). This record has the register's own coordinates (N 45.859174 W 123.856190 = 45.85933, -123.85696 on the FFLA list). Suggest merging the two, keeping these coordinates, and moving the register photo (Karl Helser, 2014) across. Elevation: the register gives 871 m (2,858 ft) and firelookout.com gives 2858 ft, but elevation_m is null here and elevation is not a facts key, so it is left for the editor. The 1942 letter describes an earlier try-out with no date, so the story does not give a start date. The 1930s end date is a decade only; no event is recorded for it. Access comes from SummitPost, which also gives approach directions to private land; no route is repeated. Not read: the register nominator (Tammy McLeod) and any Oregon Department of Forestry record for the 1921 build.
